Annual Ceremony and Poetry Reading
Fall 2026
Jennifer Chang will be coming back to CGU in the fall for a week of poetry events. Keep an eye out for more news soon!
2026
Jennifer Chang (An Authentic Life, Copper Canyon Press), whose sprawling yet urgent collection interrogates the philosophical and political “fathers” at the center of Western history and was a finalist for both the National Book Critics Circle Award and the Pulitzer Prize in Poetry, is the winner of the $100,000 Kingsley Tufts Award. Eduardo Martínez-Leyva (Cowboy Park, University of Wisconsin Press), whose debut reclaims the mythology of the American cowboy through a queer, Latinx lens while bearing witness to the violence and resilience of life on the border — and which won both the Felix Pollak Prize in Poetry and the Lambda Literary Award for LGBTQ+ Poetry — is the winner of the $10,000 Kate Tufts Discovery Award. Congratulations to this year’s winners!
2025
Jaswinder Bolina ( English as a Second Language , Copper Canyon Press) is the winner of the $100,000 Kingsley Tufts Award, and Ariana Benson ( Black Pastoral , University of Georgia Press) is the winner of the $10,000 Kate Tufts Discovery Award. Congratulations to this year’s winners!
2024
Paisley Rekdal ( West: A Translation , Copper Canyon Press) is the winner of the $100,000 Kinglsey Tufts Award, and Jacqui Germain ( Bittering the Wound , Autumn House Press) is the winner of the $10,000 Kate Tufts Discovery Award. Read more about both award recipients .
2022
(Left photo) Divya Victor, winner of the Kingsley Tufts Poetry Award.
(Right photo) torrin a. greathouse, winner of the Kate Tufts Discovery Award.

2020
Tiana Clark, winner of the 2020 Kate Tufts Discovery Award, returned to Claremont to celebrate her award along with the 2022 winners. A special award celebration and reading took place on April 19, 2022 at the Benton Museum of Art of Pomona College to honor the 2020 & 2021 Tufts Poetry recipients.
